lines.text: Do you know how an email finds the right inbox, out of billions?
You hit send to sam at bakery dot com. Your email leaves for your own mail server first.
Your server only knows the name after the at sign, so it asks the internet's phone book, called DNS: who handles mail for bakery dot com?
DNS points to a signpost called an MX record, with the address of the bakery's mail server.
Your server hands the email over, and these days that hop is usually encrypted.
At the door, filters check it's really from you, and sniff it for spam.
Then the name before the at sign picks the inbox. Ding! Sam's got mail.
Orbi Transfer skips all of that. No address, no inbox, no account. Your file just pops up on screens nearby, locked with a code.
